register.access_notes: NOT VERIFIED - the register refuses every client I am permitted to use. Plain HTTPS GETs with an honest, self-identifying user agent ('canon-legislation-indexer/1.0 ... michael.fairweather@gmail.com') to https://laws.yukon.ca/, https://legislation.yukon.ca/, https://laws.yukon.ca/cms/table-of-public-statutes.html, https://laws.yukon.ca/cms/answers-to-common-questions.html and a statute PDF path all returned HTTP 403 with the response headers 'Server: cloudflare' and 'Cf-Mitigated: challenge'. The rest of the Government of Yukon's web estate behaves the same way: https://yukon.ca/, https://yukon.ca/en/legislation, https://www.gov.yk.ca/legislation/ and https://yukonassembly.ca/ all returned 403 from the same challenge. Only https://open.yukon.ca/ (the open-data portal, which does not carry consolidated statutes) answered 200. I then loaded https://laws.yukon.ca/ in a real browser twice - once in the sandboxed browser pane and once in the user's own ordinary Chrome, with no user-agent spoofing - and both times got the Cloudflare interstitial 'laws.yukon.ca / Performing security verification / This website uses a security service to protect against malicious bots.' It did not clear on its own after ~30 seconds of waiting in either browser; a screenshot shows a Cloudflare Turnstile 'verify you are human' widget awaiting a click. Solving or clicking through a bot challenge is out of bounds under the access rules, so I stopped there. About 10 fetch attempts in total, spaced roughly 2 seconds apart. CanLII was not used (it refuses this network). Consequence: I could verify no Yukon Act, and could not read the register's own copyright or terms page, so the 'acts' list is empty and the licence is recorded as unverified rather than guessed.

licence.summary: UNVERIFIED. Yukon statutes are subject to Crown copyright in right of the Government of Yukon, and the Yukon King's Printer sets the reproduction terms, but I could not reach the register's copyright or terms-of-use page (the whole laws.yukon.ca host is behind a Cloudflare bot challenge), so nothing here is verified and no quote can be given. A human must open laws.yukon.ca in an ordinary browser session, clear the challenge, and read the site's copyright/terms page and its 'answers to common questions' page (which is where the register explains that the official version of an Act is the paper copy published by the King's Printer, and that the online consolidations are unofficial). Do not assume an open licence: no Yukon open-government licence for legislation was verified.

Yukon (Canada).language_authenticity: UNVERIFIED on the register. Yukon's Languages Act (a Yukon statute) recognises English and French, and Yukon's First Nations languages, but I could not reach laws.yukon.ca to confirm what the register itself says about the language(s) in which Acts are enacted and published or whether both language versions are equally authoritative. Note that Yukon is not in the same position as NWT or Nunavut: its Acts are, in practice, enacted and published in English, with French versions provided for some statutes. register.name: Legislation of the Northwest Territories - the consolidated statutes and regulations service of the Legislation Division, Department of Justice, Government of the Northwest Territories
register.access_notes: Fetched over plain HTTPS with an honest, self-identifying user agent ('canon-legislation-indexer/1.0 (legislation metadata indexing; michael.fairweather@gmail.com)'). No block, no bot challenge, no rate limiting, no CAPTCHA - every request returned 200. About 14 requests in total, spaced roughly 2 seconds apart: the A-Z index page (one page, 739 KB, carrying all 239 consolidated Acts plus their regulations as a file-browser list), both paginated halves of the site's terms of use (/en/terms-of-use/ and /en/terms-of-use/page/2/), the 'Acts of the Northwest Territories - Administering Departments' table (dated October 13, 2025), and the consolidated PDFs of the nine Acts listed below plus the Official Languages Act. The register publishes each consolidation only as a PDF; there is no per-Act HTML page. The index shows, for each consolidation, a 'Modified Date' - the date of that consolidation - and each PDF's cover page prints the Act's chapter citation, its commencement, and the full chain of amending chapters with their in-force dates. The site's own disclaimer states that 'These consolidations are updated monthly and may not be the most current version available' and that the consolidations 'have been prepared for convenience of reference only, and are not an official statement of the law'; the authoritative text is the Revised Statutes of the Northwest Territories, 1988 and the Annual Volumes of the Statutes of the Northwest Territories. CanLII was not used (it refuses this network).

licence.summary: Not open. Crown copyright in right of the Government of the Northwest Territories is asserted over the whole site, legislation included, and the terms grant only non-commercial reproduction with acknowledgement. Commercial use or reproduction requires prior written consent from the Department of Justice's Communications Unit. Nothing in the terms permits adaptation, modification or the creation of derivative works - the permission given is to 'reproduce or redistribute', not to alter - so converting the statutes into a machine-readable encoding and publishing it is not covered and would need written permission. open_licence is therefore false. The GNWT's separate disclaimer also stresses that the online consolidations are not an official statement of the law.
licence.attribution: Government of the Northwest Territories copyright must be acknowledged on any non-commercial reproduction or redistribution. Suggested form: (c) Government of the Northwest Territories, Department of Justice, Legislation Division.
licence.quote: Material may not be used or reproduced for commercial purposes without the prior written consent arranged by the Department's Communications Unit. If it is reproduced or redistributed for non-commercial purposes, the Government of the Northwest Territories copyright is to be acknowledged.

Northwest Territories (Canada).language_authenticity: The Northwest Territories has eleven official languages, but statutes are authentic in two. Verified on the register's own consolidation of the Official Languages Act, RSNWT 1988, c.O-1: s. 4 provides that 'Chipewyan, Cree, English, French, Gwich'in, Inuinnaqtun, Inuktitut, Inuvialuktun, North Slavey, South Slavey and Tlicho are the Official Languages of the Northwest Territories', and s. 7(1) provides that 'Acts of the Legislature and records and journals of the Legislative Assembly shall be printed and published in English and French and both language versions are equally authoritative.' Every consolidated Act PDF on the register is accordingly bilingual English/French, with the French title and citation printed facing the English on the cover page (e.g. 'EMPLOYMENT STANDARDS ACT / SNWT 2007,c.13' facing 'LOI SUR LES NORMES D'EMPLOI / LTNO 2007, ch. 13'). The other nine official languages have status for services and in the Legislative Assembly, not as authentic versions of the statutes.

acts.title: Employment Standards Act
acts.verified_how: Fetched the register's A-Z index (https://www.justice.gov.nt.ca/en/legislation/), which lists 'Employment Standards Act' with a consolidation (Modified) date of September 21, 2026, then fetched the consolidation itself. Its cover page prints the citation the register uses - 'EMPLOYMENT STANDARDS ACT / SNWT 2007,c.13 / In force April 1, 2008; SI-002-2008' (French: 'LOI SUR LES NORMES D'EMPLOI / LTNO 2007, ch. 13') - followed by the amendment chain down to SNWT 2023,c.7[E]. Not marked repealed. Currency statement, from the register's disclaimer: 'These consolidations are updated monthly and may not be the most current version available', and this consolidation is 'not an official statement of the law... an office consolidation prepared by Legislation Division, Department of Justice, for convenience only.'
acts.notes: Wage payment, minimum wage, hours and overtime. Federally regulated employers in the NWT (banking, interprovincial transport, telecommunications) are under the Canada Labour Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. L-2 instead. The register separately lists a Payroll Tax Act, but that is a tax on remuneration, not a wage-payment statute; it is noted under Personal tax/withholding.

acts.title: Northern Employee Benefits Services Pension Plan Act
acts.verified_how: Register index entry 'Northern Employee Benefits Services Pension Plan Act', consolidation date April 1, 2025. The consolidation's cover page prints 'NORTHERN EMPLOYEE BENEFITS SERVICES PENSION PLAN ACT / SNWT 2015,c.6 / In force October 1, 2015 / SI-005-2015' (French: 'LOI SUR LE REGIME DE PENSION DES NORTHERN EMPLOYEE BENEFITS SERVICES / LTNO 2015, ch. 6'), amended by SNWT 2018,c.13 (in force January 8, 2019; SI-015-2018), SNWT 2021,c.16 (in force September 30, 2023; SI-003-2023) and SNWT 2024,c.9[F]. Cover page carries the standard notice: 'This consolidation is not an official statement of the law. It is an office consolidation prepared by Legislation Division, Department of Justice, for convenience only.' Not marked repealed. Administering department, per the register's 'Administering Departments' table dated October 13, 2025: Finance.
acts.notes: This is the territory's own pension statute: it governs the multi-employer pension plan covering employees of NWT (and Nunavut) municipalities, housing associations, health authorities and similar northern public bodies. Canada's contributory public pensions are federal and out of scope: Canada Pension Plan, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-8 and Old Age Security Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. O-9. GNWT public servants are in the federal public service plan. The register also carries a Legislative Assembly Retiring Allowances Act and a Supplementary Retiring Allowances Act, but those cover only MLAs.

acts.title: Income Tax Act

I-1'), with the amendment chain beginning SNWT 1988,c.19(Supp.) and running forward, each with its in-force date. Standard office-consolidation notice; not marked repealed. acts.notes: This is the territorial income tax Act, named as required. NWT personal income tax is levied under it and collected by the Canada Revenue Agency under a federal-territorial collection agreement; the register separately lists an Income Tax Collection Agreement Questions Act for disputes about that agreement. The federal Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.) governs the computation of income and source withholding itself. The NWT also levies a payroll tax on remuneration earned in the territory under the Payroll Tax Act, listed separately on the same register (consolidation date November 23, 2023) - relevant to withholding, but not chosen as the principal Act for this topic.

register.name: Nunavut Legislation website (Consolidated Law of Nunavut) - Legislation Division, Department of Justice, Government of Nunavut; official consolidations are published by authority of the Nunavut Territorial Printer under the Legislation Act
register.access_notes: Fetched over plain HTTPS with an honest, self-identifying user agent ('canon-legislation-indexer/1.0 (legislation metadata indexing; michael.fairweather@gmail.com)'). The site is Drupal 10 behind Cloudflare. About 37 requests in total, spaced roughly 2 seconds apart, and all but one returned 200: the home page, the 'Welcome to the Nunavut Legislation website' page (which carries the reproduction terms), the 'Current Consolidated Statutes and Regulations' index and its per-letter pages (?title=C,E,H,I,L,N,O,P,Q,R,S,U), the per-Act pages for the nine Acts below, five 'Notice under subsection 65(2) of the Legislation Act' PDFs, and the consolidation PDFs themselves (served from /en/file-download/download/public/<id>). ONE BLOCK to record: the letter-W page, https://www.nunavutlegislation.ca/en/consolidated-law/current?title=W, returned a Cloudflare interstitial ('Just a moment...', noindex/nofollow, Turnstile challenge) instead of the listing. I did not retry it and did not attempt to solve the challenge; nothing in my final selection depends on a W-letter Act (the Workers' Compensation Act was therefore not checked). Everything else was reachable. The register gives, for each Act, an English page plus Francais and, for some Acts, Inuktitut and Inuinnaqtun versions; the consolidation PDF's cover page prints the C.S.Nu. chapter citation and the consolidation date, and where the consolidation has been overtaken the Act's page carries a red 'Note: This consolidation is not up to date. See subsequent amendments: ...' with links to the amending chapters. CanLII was not used (it refuses this network).

licence.summary: Not open, though more permissive in tone than most. The Department of Justice states that, to ensure access to the laws of Nunavut, the statutes and regulations, their consolidations, and the carried-over NWT statutes and regulations as adopted for Nunavut 'may be copied freely for personal use', with no permission needed and no fee. That permission is expressly limited to personal use, and the electronic versions may not be copied for resale without the written consent of the Territorial Printer. Nothing grants a right to adapt, modify or make derivative works, and nothing covers non-personal (e.g. organisational or public re-publication) use - so a machine-readable re-encoding published for others would fall outside the permission and needs the Territorial Printer's written consent. open_licence is therefore false. Note also the status split the register makes: an 'Official Consolidation of ...' is published under the Legislation Act and is an official statement of the law subject to s. 66(2), while a plain 'Consolidation of ...' is expressly unofficial.
licence.attribution: No attribution formula is prescribed for personal-use copying. Contact for anything beyond it: Nunavut Official Editor / Territorial Printer, Legislation Division, Department of Justice, Government of Nunavut (Territorial.Printer@gov.nu.ca). Suggested credit: Government of Nunavut, Department of Justice, Legislation Division.
licence.quote: There is no requirement to seek permission and there are no fees to be paid for reproductions of the statutes and regulations for personal use. The electronic versions of the statutes and regulations may not be copied for the purpose of resale in this or any other form without the written consent of the Territorial Printer.

Nunavut (Canada).language_authenticity: Three official languages, but only two authentic statute versions by default. Verified on the register's own Official Consolidation of the Official Languages Act, C.S.Nu., c.O-20 (in force April 1, 2013, SI-001-2013; current to September 18, 2025): s. 3(1) 'Inuktut, English and French are the Official Languages of Nunavut', and s. 5(1) 'The Acts of the Legislature shall be made, printed and published in English and French and both versions are equally authoritative.' The Inuit language does not automatically carry statute-authenticity: s. 5(2) requires an Inuktitut version of a bill to be available when the bill is introduced, s. 5(3) lets the Commissioner in Executive Council order an Inuktut version of an Act to be published, and s. 5(4) provides that the Legislative Assembly, on the recommendation of the Executive Council, may by resolution designate an Inuktut version of an Act to be authoritative. So Inuktut versions have official status only where so designated, Act by Act. In practice the register offers Francais on essentially every Act page and Inuktitut (and, for some Acts such as the Official Languages Act itself, Inuinnaqtun) on a subset. 'Inuktut' is the current statutory term, substituted for 'the Inuit Language' by S.Nu. 2025, c.22, s.45(1); the companion statute is now the Inuktut Protection Act (formerly the Inuit Language Protection Act).

acts.title: Labour Standards Act
acts.identifier: C.S.Nu., c.L-10 (originating as R.S.N.W.T. 1988, c.L-1, duplicated for Nunavut)
acts.verified_how: Fetched the register's per-Act page, titled 'LABOUR STANDARDS ACT, Official Consolidation of', listed under L in the Current Consolidated Statutes and Regulations. Its legal notice PDF (noticeCSNucL10.pdf) is headed 'Labour Standards Act / C.S.Nu.,c.L-10 / Notice under subsection 65(2) of the Legislation Act' and records changes 'made in the June 13, 2022 consolidation'. The consolidation PDF's cover page prints 'OFFICIAL CONSOLIDATION OF LABOUR STANDARDS ACT / C.S.Nu.,c.L-10 / (Consolidation date: June 13, 2022) / R.S.N.W.T. 1988,c.L-1', then 'AS AMENDED BY NORTHWEST TERRITORIES STATUTES', 'AS AMENDED BY STATUTES ENACTED UNDER SECTION 76.05 OF NUNAVUT ACT' (S.N.W.T. 1998,c.38, in force April 1, 1999) and 'AS AMENDED BY NUNAVUT STATUTES'. In force; not repealed. Currency caveat printed by the register on the Act's own page: 'This consolidation is not up to date. See subsequent amendments: S.Nu. 2022,c.14,s.5 and S.Nu. 2023,c.16,s.111.'
acts.notes: Carried-over NWT statute: the Act in force in Nunavut is the Northwest Territories Labour Standards Act, R.S.N.W.T. 1988, c.L-1, duplicated for Nunavut on division day under the Nunavut Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. 28 (2nd Supp.)), since amended by Nunavut's own Legislature and now consolidated as C.S.Nu., c.L-10. Nunavut kept the older 'Labour Standards' title; the NWT replaced its version with the Employment Standards Act, S.N.W.T. 2007, c.13, in 2008, so the two territories' employment-standards law has diverged. Wage payment and minimum wage. Federally regulated employers in Nunavut are under the Canada Labour Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. L-2.

It still carries its NWT chapter citation because it has not yet been given a C.S.Nu. chapter number, and the register publishes it only as an unofficial 'Consolidation of', not an 'Official Consolidation of'. Unemployment benefits are federal (Employment Insurance Act, S.C. 1996, c. 23), as are the Canada Child Benefit and GST credit. Nunavut also has a Senior Citizens Benefits Act and a Collaboration for Poverty Reduction Act on the same register.

acts.title: Income Tax Act
acts.identifier: C.S.Nu., c.I-20 (originating as R.S.N.W.T. 1988, c.I-1, duplicated for Nunavut)
acts.verified_how: Register page 'INCOME TAX ACT, Official Consolidation of', listed under I, with legal notice last updated 01 June 2026. The notice PDF (NoticeCSNucI20.pdf) is headed 'Income Tax Act / C.S.Nu.,c.I-20 / Notice under subsection 65(2) of the Legislation Act' and records changes 'made in the September 18, 2025 consolidation'. The consolidation PDF's cover prints 'OFFICIAL CONSOLIDATION OF INCOME TAX ACT / C.S.Nu.,c.I-20 / (Consolidation date: September 18, 2025) / R.S.N.W.T. 1988,c.I-1'. In force; not repealed. Currency caveat on the Act's page: 'This consolidation is not up to date. See subsequent amendments: S.Nu. 2026,c.8.'
acts.notes: This is the territorial income tax Act, named as required. Carried-over NWT statute: the Northwest Territories Income Tax Act, R.S.N.W.T. 1988, c.I-1, duplicated for Nunavut and since amended by the Nunavut Legislature, now consolidated as C.S.Nu., c.I-20. Nunavut personal income tax is levied under it and collected by the Canada Revenue Agency under a federal-territorial collection agreement; the register separately lists an Income Tax Collection Agreement Questions Act. Computation of income and source withholding themselves are federal (Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.)). Nunavut also levies a payroll tax on remuneration earned in the territory under the Payroll Tax Act, listed separately on the same register as an unofficial consolidation.

acts.title: Insurance Act
acts.identifier: C.S.Nu., c.I-40 (originating as R.S.N.W.T. 1988, c.I-4, duplicated for Nunavut)
acts.verified_how: Register page 'INSURANCE ACT, Official Consolidation of', listed under I, legal notice last updated 03 July 2025. The notice PDF (NoticeCSNucI-40E.pdf) is headed 'Insurance Act / C.S.Nu.,c.I-40 / Notice under subsection 65(2) of the Legislation Act' and records changes 'made in the July 3, 2025 consolidation' (including replacing 'the Territories' with 'Nunavut' in the definitions in s. 1(1), a tell-tale of the carried-over origin). The consolidation PDF's cover prints 'OFFICIAL CONSOLIDATION OF INSURANCE ACT / C.S.Nu.,c.I-40 / (Consolidation date: July 3, 2025) / R.S.N.W.T. 1988,c.I-4'. In force; not repealed. Currency caveat on the Act's page: 'This consolidation is not up to date. See subsequent amendments: S.Nu. 2025,c.23,s.35 and S.Nu. 2026,c.7,s.9.'
acts.notes: Carried-over NWT statute (R.S.N.W.T. 1988, c.I-4), duplicated for Nunavut under the Nunavut Act and since amended by Nunavut. Statutory conditions, proof of loss, claims payment and insurer licensing. Work injury compensation is separate (Workers' Compensation Act; note that the register's letter-W listing could not be retrieved - see access_notes - so that Act was not verified).

acts.title: Utility Rates Review Council Act
acts.verified_how: Register page 'UTILITY RATES REVIEW COUNCIL ACT, Consolidation of', listed under U in the Current Consolidated Statutes and Regulations. The consolidation PDF's cover prints 'CONSOLIDATION OF UTILITY RATES REVIEW COUNCIL ACT / S.Nu. 2001,c.3 / In force March 31, 2001, except s.22 / s.22 in force March 30, 2001 / (Current to: October 14, 2010)', amended by S.Nu. 2010,c.3,s.18 and S.Nu. 2010,c.6 (in force March 23, 2010). Its running footer repeats 'Utility Rates Review Council Act, Consolidation of - Current to: 2010-10-14'. Its table of contents shows the operative headings 'PROPOSED RATES AND TARIFFS', 'Imposition of rates and tariffs' (s. 12.1), 'Application for approval of rate or tariff' and 'Interim rate or tariff'. Cross-checked against the Official Consolidation of the Qulliq Energy Corporation Act, C.S.Nu., c.Q-20 (consolidation date November 7, 2024), whose s. 5(e) empowers the corporation 'subject to the Utility Rates Review Council Act, to set rates and tariffs' - confirming this Act as the rate-setting control. In force; not repealed.
acts.notes: A Nunavut statute of its own (not carried over). Nunavut has no Public Utilities Act and no standing utilities board: this Act creates the Utility Rates Review Council, which reviews and advises on rate and tariff applications, with approval resting with the responsible Minister/Executive Council. The utility itself is constituted by the Qulliq Energy Corporation Act, C.S.Nu., c.Q-20 - an Official Consolidation, and itself a carried-over NWT Act (R.S.N.W.T. 1988, c.N-2, the former Northwest Territories Power Corporation Act). CAUTION: this Act is published only as an UNOFFICIAL consolidation and the register's own text is current only to 14 October 2010, so amendments after that date are not reflected.

acts.title: Residential Tenancies Act
acts.identifier: C.S.Nu., c.R-60 (originating as R.S.N.W.T. 1988, c.R-5, duplicated for Nunavut)
acts.verified_how: Register page 'RESIDENTIAL TENANCIES ACT, Official Consolidation of', listed under R, legal notice last updated 13 December 2024. The notice PDF (NoticeCSNucR60.pdf) is headed 'Residential Tenancies Act / C.S.Nu.,c.R-60 / Notice under subsection 65(2) of the Legislation Act' and records changes 'made in the May 31, 2024 consolidation'. The consolidation PDF's cover prints 'OFFICIAL CONSOLIDATION OF RESIDENTIAL TENANCIES ACT / C.S.Nu.,c.R-60 / (Consolidation date: May 31, 2024) / R.S.N.W.T. 1988,c.R-5'. In force; not repealed; the Act's page carries no 'not up to date' warning.
acts.notes: Carried-over NWT statute (R.S.N.W.T. 1988, c.R-5), duplicated for Nunavut under the Nunavut Act and since amended by Nunavut. Rent, deposits, repairs, termination and the Rental Officer's jurisdiction; it matters unusually much in Nunavut, where most housing is public or staff housing. The general consumer statute for the same topic is the Consumer Protection Act, verified on the same register as an 'Official Consolidation of' under C; only one Act is listed per topic and tenancy was chosen as the more consequential everyday statute.

topic_gaps.reason: Federal, not territorial. Air carriage and passenger compensation are governed by the Canada Transportation Act, S.C. 1996, c. 10 and the Air Passenger Protection Regulations, SOR/2019-150, administered by the Canadian Transportation Agency. This bites harder in Nunavut than anywhere else in Canada - every community is fly-in - but it remains entirely federal; the register's Public Highways Act and Motor Vehicles legislation do not touch compensation for delayed or denied carriage.
Federal and exclusive. Constitution Act, 1867, s. 91(2)-(3); Customs Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (2nd Supp.) and Customs Tariff, S.C. 1997, c. 36. A territory cannot legislate customs duties.

Federal. Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, S.C. 2001, c. 27 and the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, SOR/2002-227 govern entry, status and work authorisation. Nunavut has no territorial immigration statute and, unlike the other territories, has historically not run a provincial/territorial nominee program of its own.
